text:
anya: Quick heads-up — I ran an nsys capture on the canary repro for the KV cache perf regression. Used trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt and kept it short (30s) to get a broad view.
sam: cool. which nsys flags did you pick? last time we blew up the qdrep by capturing everything.
anya: I started with:
``nys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=30 --output=kv-regress-30s --force true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi``
(typo in the example above — actual command was `nsys profile`).
cheng: fwiw `--sample=cpu` reduces OSRT event noise but doesn't stop lots of tiny GPU kernel slices when the workload has many short requests. 30s on 80GB runs generates a lot of tiny events.
perf-bot: :robot_face: Auto-report: capture size 1.2GB; nvtx regions found under /srv/runtime/*; top GPU consumer: cudnn_convolution (~42% aggregate GPU time).
kai: did the trace show clear batching spikes or was it a smear? last time overlapping kernels confused our KV eviction metrics.
anya: timeline shows repeating pattern: tiny KV lookup memcpy kernels, a `fast_path_dispatch` entry/exit NVTX pair, then long cudnn_convolution runs. Between the memcpys and conv there are extra small kernels attributed to the kernel-selection shim. that shim call wasn't present in prod traces earlier.
leah: we toggled `batch_split_threshold_ms` in the sampler last week. if small batches are split earlier, that could cause extra dispatches and separate memcpys.
sam: can you paste the NVTX sequence around a spike? i'll grep for `kv_` names in the .qdrep.
anya: snippet from NVTX capture (copied directly):
``
NVTX: KVCACHE_LKUP start
NVTX: fast_path_dispatch enter
NVTX: mem_copy_kv_to_gpu
NVTX: fast_path_dispatch exit
NVTX: cudnn_convolution exec
```
cheng: that `mem_copy_kv_to_gpu` being a separate small memcpy is suspicious — we expect one batched memcpy for the whole micro-batch. looks like dispatch didn't merge prefixes.
kai: hypothesis: when prefix_length < 32 tokens we take `path A` (no prefetch batching). if multiple concurrent short-prefix requests arrive, dispatch doesn't merge them so we get N small memcpys instead of 1.
anya: i re-ran two quick captures: one with `--sample=cpu` and duration=30, another with `--duration=10` and removed `--sample=cpu` and set `--sample-interval=0.5ms` for OSRT. the 10s capture produced crisper kernel boundaries and clearly showed separate small memcpy kernels rather than a single consolidated memcpy.
leah: mitigation idea: set `batching.merge_window_ms` to 1.5ms so short arrivals within that window get merged, and add a runtime counter for `fast_path_dispatch` calls/sec to monitor effect.
sam: also run `nsys stats kv-regress-30s.qdrep --report=gpu` and grep for `memcpy HtoD` to count memcpy invocations; that'll quantify how many separate copies happened.
perf-bot: :chart_with_upwards_trend: suggestion: add a short periodic profiler job on canary (5s captures, `--trace=cuda,osrt`) with a rolling retention of 3 captures so we can reproduce small traces quickly.
anya: i'll open a tiny PR to tweak the sampler heuristic and add the `fast_path_dispatch` metric; i'll attach the 10s and 30s qdrep files in the PR and link them in the changelist. uploads will go to /artifacts/perf/1959991111/. :thumbsup:
cheng: once PR lands i can run a dedicated repro and measure p50/p95 latency and total memcpy counts to ensure no latency regression.
anya: thanks — will post updates here when captures are uploaded and ci runs finish.
